slides.topic: Non-communicable Diseases — Risk, Prevention & Multimorbidity — source 3
slides.text:
Why are we interested? 
Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) kill 41 million people each year, equivalent to 60% of all deaths globally.
Each year, 17 million people die from a NCD before age 70; 
Of all NCD deaths, 77% are in low and middle-income countries.
Cardiovascular diseases account for most NCD deaths, or 17.9 million people annually, followed by cancers (9.3 million), chronic respiratory diseases (4.1 million), and diabetes (2.0 million including kidney disease deaths caused by diabetes).
These four groups of diseases account for over 80% of all premature NCD deaths.

https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/noncommunicable-diseases

slides.topic: Non-communicable Diseases — Risk, Prevention & Multimorbidity — source 4
slides.text:
Multiple long-term conditions (MLTC): Living with two or more chronic illnesses. For example, a person could have diabetes, heart disease and depression at the same time. 

Multimorbidity can have a significant impact on people's health and wellbeing. It also poses a complex challenge to healthcare systems which are traditionally focused on individual diseases.

Multiple long-term conditions are much more common in older people, affecting more than half of those over 65, however, they can also be found in young people.

Khunti K, Sathanapally H, Mountain P. (2023) Multiple long term conditions, multimorbidity, and co-morbidities: we should reconsider the terminology we use. BMJ. Oct 13;383:2327
Multimorbidity

slides.topic: Non-communicable Diseases — Risk, Prevention & Multimorbidity — source 5
slides.text:
Who is at risk? 
People of all age groups, regions and countries are affected by NCDs. These conditions are often associated with older age groups, but data shows that 17 million NCD deaths occur before the age of 70 years. 
https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/noncommunicable-diseases

NCD Countdown 2030 collaborators (2018). NCD Countdown 2030: worldwide trends in non-communicable disease mortality and progress towards Sustainable Development Goal target 3.4. Lancet. Sep 22;392(10152):1072-1088.

slides.topic: Non-communicable Diseases — Risk, Prevention & Multimorbidity — source 6
slides.text:
What is their aetiology?
What is the cause of these diseases?
A combination of physiological, environmental, behavioural and genetic factors.

NCDs are driven by forces that include rapid, unplanned urbanization, globalization leading to unhealthy lifestyles.

Ageing population

Socioeconomic impact/poverty

Behaviour (often emerge during childhood and adolescence).

slides.topic: Non-communicable Diseases — Risk, Prevention & Multimorbidity — source 7
slides.text:
What are the risk factors for NCD’s?
What is a risk factor?


Modifiable:  Can be changed, controlled, or influenced through interventions or lifestyle adjustments.

Non-modifiable: These factors are inherent or fixed and serve as baseline risks that individuals carry

A characteristic, condition, or behaviour that increases the likelihood of getting a disease or injury.

Modifiable are the major risk factors for the most common NCDs
Smoking, physical inactivity, unhealthy diet and the harmful use of alcohol, all increase the risk of NCDs.
Tobacco accounts for over 8 million deaths every year (including from the effects of exposure to second-hand smoke) (1).
1.8 million annual deaths have been attributed to excess salt/sodium intake (1).
830 000 deaths annually can be attributed to insufficient physical activity (1).

Non-modifiable: Age, gender, family history, ethnicity

(1) https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/

slides.topic: Non-communicable Diseases — Risk, Prevention & Multimorbidity — source 8
slides.text:
The World Health Organization has estimated that if the major risk factors for chronic disease were eliminated, at least 80% of all heart disease, stroke, and type 2 diabetes would be prevented, and more than 40% of cancer cases would be prevented.

World Health Organization. Preventing chronic diseases: a vital investment. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2005. Available from: http://www.who.int/chp/chronic_disease_report/full_report.pdf
NCDs are among the most common and costly of all health problems: However, they are also among the most preventable.
